gbm_population_evidence.quote: Malignant Brain Tumor; Malignant Glioma; Embryonal Tumor
diagnosis of supra-tentorial primary malignant brain tumor (e.g. malignant glioma, embryonal tumor including ATRT, ependymoma)

candidate_evidence.quote: The opening of the BBB with the SonoCloud-9 system will increase the tumor exposure to carboplatin and increase progression-free and overall survival in pediatric patients treated for a recurrent malignant supra-tentorial brain tumor.
indication of treatment with carboplatin, validated in multidisciplinary meeting

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: recurrence or progression of brain tumor after at least a first line of standard treatment (multifocal tumors and metastatic disease allowed)

role_evidence.quote: the blood-brain barrier can be transiently and safely opened with pulsed low intensity ultrasound immediately prior to intravenously delivered chemotherapy
Clinical efficacy of BBB disruption by the SonoCloud® device in association with systemic chemotherapy: Overall Survival (OS)
in relation to the use of the ultrasound contrast agent SonoVue® for BBB disruption in the pediatric population

agents.drug_class_hint: ultrasound contrast agent (sulfur hexafluoride microbubbles) used for BBB opening

source_quote.quote: DNA and tumor cells concentrations in blood and cerebrospinal fluid

coder_notes: Paediatric-only trial (Ages: CHILD; 5 to <18 years), so it should fail S4 by [CODE]; coded in full anyway. Glioblastoma is not named in conditions, title or inclusion criteria (only 'malignant glioma'); glioblastoma appears only in the detailed description about a prior adult trial. Carboplatin is not a registered intervention (only the SonoCloud device is) but every patient receives it and its ultrasound-enabled delivery is the study question, so it is coded as a device-dependent candidate (C12/R5). SonoVue microbubbles are delivery-enabling. ctDNA in blood/CSF is an ancillary correlative measure.
